subject: URGENT: Elevated 5xx/429 and retry amplification — RetailX production
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <ops@retailx.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T18:23:00Z
Subject: High 5xx/429 on /v1/generate - seeing retries

Evelyn,

We're seeing a sharp spike in 5xx and 429s from Redwood on our production traffic starting ~18:10 UTC. Traffic looks normal on our side; errors correlate with increased upstream retries from our proxy (we're seeing amplified retries that quickly exhaust our egress).

Quick details:
- Endpoint: POST /v1/generate
- Error mix: ~65% 5xx (502/503) and ~25% 429s
- Region: us-east-1
- Impact: ~40% failed requests; user-facing errors on checkout flow

I've attached a small set of proxy logs and a Grafana snapshot. Please advise immediate mitigation steps — we need something that avoids further retry amplification.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
SRE, RetailX

Attachment: proxy-logs-20260814.zip (12MB gzipped logs)
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <ops@retailx.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T18:31:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 on /v1/generate - seeing retries

Samantha — thanks for the alert and logs. We're on it. Initial triage notes:
- We see a correlated spike in our egress errors to Route53 + increased connection resets from a subset of gw-proxy nodes.
- Our telemetry shows a backlog forming in the frontend proxies which then retry aggressively into the serving fleet (KV cache timeouts + transient 5xx).

Immediate actions we're taking now (I will update every 20 mins):
1) Apply a temporary client-side backoff at the proxy tier (global killswitch to reduce max retries from 5 -> 1).
2) Route a fraction of traffic (10%) to the standby region (us-west-2) to relieve pressure.
3) Open case with AWS Route53/NOC for possible DNS throttling in the affected AZs.

Can you confirm whether RetailX can tolerate the 10% traffic split to us-west-2 for the next 2 hours? If yes, we'll start the partial failover immediately.

Evelyn Hart
Incident Lead, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T18:42:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 on /v1/generate - seeing retries

Adding some technical color:
- The proxy backoff killswitch is a low-risk toggle; it will reduce our own retries and should quickly lower overall load.
- I'm concerned about prefix cache invalidations during failover; recommend we pin RetailX to a compatible smaller sequence model instance in us-west-2 to avoid cold-KV thrash.
- Let's also enable 429->503 translation at the proxy for a short window to avoid client retry loops (we'll annotate logs so this is reversible).

I'll push the killswitch now and coordinate with SRE.

Marcus Lin
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <ops@retailx.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T18:58:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 on /v1/generate - seeing retries

Samantha — RetailX confirmed via Ops on their side that a 10% partial failover is acceptable for the next 2 hours. Initiating:
- Killswitch: applied (max retries -> 1) on all frontend proxies at 18:56 UTC.
- Traffic split: 10% sent to us-west-2 starting 18:57 UTC.
- Translation: 429->503 mapping enabled for a 30-minute window.

Early telemetry (18:58 UTC):
- Total request rate down ~12% (expected).
- 5xx rate decreased from 65% -> ~34% in the routed cohort; overall customer errors improving but still elevated.

We have an active AWS NOC ticket (see below) and we're shipping more diagnostic traces. Attaching Route53 trace.

Attachment: route53-trace-aug14.txt

Evelyn
From: AWS NOC <aws-noc@amazon.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T20:12:00Z
Subject: RE: Case #12345678 - Route53 partial throttling observed

Evelyn / team,

Thanks for the heads-up. We've identified a regional Route53 control-plane throttling event that started at 18:05 UTC impacting a subset of health-check and resolution requests in us-east-1. The control-plane is back to steady-state as of 19:45 UTC, but the client-side retries and cache expirations caused by the transient have produced amplification into downstream services.

Recommendations we made and applied:
- We increased resolver capacity in the impacted edge (no changes required on your side).
- For immediate mitigation: reduce aggressive retry policies, and allow clients to observe extended TTLs for 10 minutes post-incident.

We'll keep the ticket open for two business days and share detailed trace artifacts when available.

AWS NOC
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <ops@retailx.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:44:00Z
Subject: Incident summary and next steps — RetailX outage window 18:05-19:45 UTC

Team / Samantha — quick postmortem summary and action items:

Summary:
- Root cause: regional Route53 control-plane throttling (us-east-1) triggered transient DNS failures and cache invalidations, which in turn caused frontend proxies to aggressively retry into serving fleet. The retries amplified failures, producing elevated 5xx/429 rates and customer-visible errors on RetailX checkout flows. Incident window: ~18:05 - 19:45 UTC (spike tailing into 20:15 UTC).

Actions completed during incident:
- Applied proxy killswitch to cap retries (reduced amplification).
- Partial traffic reroute (10%) to us-west-2 to relieve pressure and allow cold-model mitigation.
- Enabled temporary 429->503 translation to avoid client-side retry loops.
- Opened AWS NOC ticket #12345678 and validated control-plane throttling event.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Engineering (marcus_lin): Add adaptive retry logic to frontend proxies (dynamic backoff based on upstream latency/5xx rate). ETA: 3 weeks.
- Infra (laura_bennett): Add synthetic DNS health-checks and alerting tied to Route53 control-plane anomalies. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Customer Success (evelyn_hart): Provide RetailX with a formal incident report and credit ask template. ETA: EOD 2026-08-16.

Attachments: grafana-spike-aug14.png (dashboard snapshot)

Samantha, let me know if you want a joint call with our VP of Infra for next-day remediation planning.

Evelyn Hart
Incident Lead, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
